messages:
tara: FYI scheduling a staggered apply for cross-region peering + IAM tweaks during the 03:00 UTC change window. This touches module=network/peers and module=iam/federation. Need provider pin and a clear rollback lane.

oscar: ack. prefer to canary region-by-region: eu-west-1 -> us-west-2 -> us-east-1. Which provider version are we pinning to?

tara: pin to registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws v4.57.2. Reason: v4.58 changed default kms_encryption behavior which caused a lambda role attach to fail in internal testbed. We'll document in release notes.

maya: deploybot: please set deploybot.pin to aws@4.57.2, suspend auto-bumps for the window, and schedule region canaries 20m apart. Also set abort thresholds based on assume-role failures and kms decrypt errors.

deploybot: deploybot: Pin applied: aws -> 4.57.2 for release/2026-09. Auto-updates paused until 2026-09-05T00:00:00Z. Schedule: eu-west-1 2026-09-04T02:20:00Z, us-west-2 2026-09-04T02:40:00Z, us-east-1 2026-09-04T03:00:00Z. On abort: run targeted rollback and page @oncall-eng.

ben: Preflight plan (eu-west-1 canary) shows small policy text changes and one new attachment. plan excerpt:
```
# module.network/peers
~ aws_vpc_peering_connection.peers (tags change)
# module.iam/federation
~ aws_iam_role.federation_role (policy JSON update)
+ aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.federation_attach
```
Looks safe but we should snapshot state.

tara: Agreed. Run `terraform state pull > state.pre.eu-west-1.json` and upload to s3://redwood-backups/state-snapshots/ before each region apply.

maya: Abort thresholds: trigger abort if (assume_role_errors OR kms_decrypt_errors) > 0.03 across canary instances for a 5m sliding window. On abort: deploybot will pin to previous provider (aws@4.56.9), kick targeted apply to revert module.

deplybot: (typo correction) deploybot: thresholds set as requested. On abort: pin->4.56.9, run `terraform apply -target=module.iam/federation -var-file=rollback.vars -auto-approve` on the commit tagged `pre-2026-09-04` and post to #eng-oncall.

sre-bot: SRE monitoring will subscribe to metrics: `iam.assume_error_rate`, `kms.decrypt_error_rate`, and `lambda.attach_failures`. We'll post an aggregated graph in the release message.

oscar: Rollback options documented: 
Plan A (fast revert): apply previous policy from git tag `release/pre-2026-09-04` targeting only `module.iam/federation`.
Plan B (partial mitigation): if only peering tags are the culprit, run `aws ec2 modify-vpc-peering-connection-options` to revert tag-based routing flags and avoid full revert.
Plan C (nuclear): restore Terraform state snapshot and run an apply from that commit; only if metadata/attachments are inconsistent and Plan A fails.

ben: note about release notes: include the provider rationale, regions and timing, post-deploy checks (1) cross-account assume works, (2) peering traffic flows between regions, (3) CI pipelines using federation role succeed. Add runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/infra-apply-backout

tara: primary on-call for the window = @tara, backup = @maya. I will post a 15m preflight in #eng-infra with the plan and the SRE dashboard link.

maya: small nit: use `terraform plan -out=region.plan -target=module.iam/federation --refresh=false` for canaries to speed test and reduce noise.

sre-bot: Confirmed: we'll watch the 5m sliding windows and will automatically page if errors cross threshold. We'll also keep an open channel in #incident-response.

ben: one more ops-safety: don't run a full `terraform apply` on prod until eu-west-1 has been green for at least 15 minutes and no errors in the 15m post-apply window.

tara: ack. After eu-west-1 green for 15m we proceed to us-west-2, then wait 15m, then us-east-1. If any step fails we abort and follow Plan A. I'll attach the small diff and release note blurb before canary. End.
